title: Problem Set Part
description: One JSON file describes ONE part of a problem set. Files that share the same setId are grouped into a single problem set (one rail slot, one Submit button). See README.md for the full authoring recipe and a worked example of every type. Answer fields (answer, answers) live here on the server and are stripped out before anything is sent to the browser.

setId.description: Groups parts into one set. All five PS2 sheets use "ps2". Used in the page URL (?set=ps2) and in the API path.

setTitle.description: Human title for the whole set, shown in the rail and at the top of the activity. Put it on at least one part file in the set; the loader reads it from the first part that has it.

order.description: Which numbered rail slot this set fills (1..20). Put it on at least one part file. Omit it and set "demo": true for demo sets.

demo.description: true marks the set as a demo. Demo sets appear in a separate group below the numbered slots.

id.description: Unique id for THIS part, across the whole project. Used as the partId when checking answers.

part.description: Title of this part, shown as a section heading in the activity (for example "Concatenators").

partOrder.description: Order of this part within its set (1, 2, 3, ...).

type.description: Which renderer and which check rule to use for this part.

instructions.description: A string or an array of strings (one per line) shown above the rows.

columns.description: variable-trace ONLY. The tracked variable names, in column order (for example ["foo", "bar"]). The student fills one input per column per row.

shift.description: caesar-cipher ONLY. How many places each letter moves.

direction.description: caesar-cipher ONLY. Shown to the student and reminds them which way to shift.

rows.description: The graded rows. The exact shape depends on type. See README.md.

id.description: Unique row id within this part ("1", "2", ...).

code.description: predict-output, valid-invalid-type, variable-trace: the line of Python shown to the student.

char.description: caesar-cipher: the source character for this position.

starter.description: free-form (optional): text to prefill the input with.

answer.description: predict-output, free-form, caesar-cipher: the single correct answer. STRIPPED before sending to the client.

answers.description: valid-invalid-type and variable-trace: the correct value per field. For valid-invalid-type the keys are "validity" ("Valid" or "Invalid") and "dataType". For variable-trace the keys are the column names. STRIPPED before sending to the client.

hint.description: Optional. Encouraging nudge shown ONLY when the student gets the row wrong. Never sent until then.
